Subject: Post-call: Developer onramp — SDK quickstart & local lab plan

Hi Emma / Samir — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed hands-on plan to get AltaHealth's dev team unblocked for a first local pilot.

Call highlights:
- Goal: validate a short on-device/local developer loop for search & assistant features (embeddings + reranker + structured tool-calling).
- Primary constraints: Must run behind AltaHealth VPC for dev pre-prod, SSO-managed access, and need an internal reranker evaluation before model rollout.

Proposed local lab (minimal friction path) — 5 steps
1) Environment prep (local machine + Node/Python): venv / nvm recommendations, Docker optional.
2) Auth: ephemeral dev tokens for local testing; SSO-backed service account for CI.
3) Routing & model selection: start with a small open LLM (redwood-compact) for latency checks, fallback to higher-quality variant for rerank pipelines.
4) Embeddings + reranker: index a small sample corpus and wire a lightweight reranker using Redwood’s embeddings API + a re-ranking prompt template.
5) Structured output / tool calls: test a toy tool (calendar lookup) and a structured JSON output path to validate parsing.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart-checklist.pdf (one-page checklist) and sample-apps.zip (Python + TS sample apps — local dev mode).

Next steps / ask from AltaHealth:
- Please share the AWS account id or a dev IAM contact who can accept our sandbox role.
- Who will own SSO/Konnect provisioning? We'll need one point-of-contact to generate an initial dev service account.
- Confirm a 30-min lab slot for a guided quickstart (I suggested Wed 22 Jun 11:00 PT below).

I’ll loop in Neha (SDK lead) and Karthik (integration) to prepare the quickstart bundle and a 30-min lab script.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks

On Tue, Jun 20, 2028 at 1:45 PM Emma Ross <emma.ross@altahealth.com> wrote:
> For local dev, do you recommend running a local model container or will the SDK call your hosted endpoints?

Short answers / dev recommendations from the SDK team:
- Hosted endpoints are the fastest path for iteration. Use short-lived dev tokens for local dev to avoid long-lived keys on dev machines.
- If you need air-gapped testing, we provide a local runtime package (requires larger GPU hardware); for the PoC start with hosted endpoints + local sample apps that mock the same runtime behavior.

Environment notes (minimum):
- Python: 3.10+ (use venv); recommended packages: redwood-sdk==1.6.x, requests, uvicorn (for local tool stubs).
- Node: 18.x LTS; NPM packages: @redwood/inference (TS SDK), cross-env.
- Env vars (local dev):
  - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=\"<dev-token>\"
  - export REDWOOD_ENV=dev
  - export ALTA_SAMPLE_BUCKET=\"s3://alta-test-bucket\" (only if you plan to persist embeddings)

Quick TS example for streaming + structured output (local test):
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-compact', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Find available cardiology slots' }], response_format: 'json' });
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk.delta);
}

Structured output tip: include a JSON schema in the request and validate server-side. We also include a small parser in the sample-apps.zip under ts/structured-parser.js.

Embeddings + rerank: use the embeddings endpoint to index a small representative set (100–500 docs) and then send top-K hits into a reranker prompt; we include a reranker template in sample-apps/python/reranker_template.py.

I'll jump on the lab prep to prepare the quickstart bundle and a small checklist for infra/Security. Happy to address items in the attached questionnaire — will follow up on the token rotation/data retention rows after review.

-Neha
